EO 11299 (signed 1966-08-15; 31 FR 10917) was read in full in the held Federal Register text layer. Acting under subsection (f) of section 303 of the Government Employees Salary Reform Act of 1964, it amends section 2 of Executive Order No. 11248 of October 10, 1965, as amended, by adding item (9), Director, Urban Transportation Administration, Department of Housing and Urban Development, to level V. The packet's machine inventory also swept in the Civil Service Commission and other documents that follow the order on the same Federal Register pages (offsets 1776 to 7499, including an Excepted Service rule 'until December 31, 1967'); those are different documents, not clauses of this order, and I corrected the inventory by override to the order's single operative clause (lead plus item). EO 11604 (1971-07-02) renumbered the item (items (9) through (24) as (8) through (23)). EO 11634 (signed 1971-12-06) amended section 2 of EO 11248 by deleting item (8), Director, Urban Transportation Administration, Department of Housing and Urban Development, outright, without inserting a replacement; a deletion without replacement removes the placement, so the clause first ended on 1971-12-06 (signing date; no effective-date provision), which is also the whole-order end. The later transfer of urban mass transportation functions out of that Department (Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1968) is not held and is not used as an end: the placement stood in EO 11248 as amended, and was re-listed in numbering by EO 11604, until EO 11634 removed it, and I found no held instrument that extinguished it earlier. EO 11409 (signed 1968-04-29; 33 FR 6601) was read in full in the held Federal Register text layer. Acting under section 5317 of title 5, U.S. Code, it amends Executive Order No. 11248 of October 10, 1965, as amended. Section 1 (level IV): (a) deletes item (3), Special Assistant to the Secretary (Food-For-Peace Program), State Department, and inserts item (3), Administrator, Social and Rehabilitation Service, HEW; (b) deletes item (4), Executive Secretary of the President's Commission on Law Enforcement and Administration of Justice, and inserts item (4), Administrator, National Institutes of Health, HEW; (c) adds item (8), Administrator, Health Services and Mental Health Administration, HEW, and item (9), Executive Director, Cabinet Committee on Price Stability. Section 2 (level V) deletes item (15), Administrator, Social and Rehabilitation Service, and inserts item (15), Deputy Administrator, Health Services and Mental Health Administration. The commands that remove the earlier items (3), (4) and (15) were performed when the order took effect; the clauses below are the placements the order made, one per item, with the lead and introductions folded in. EO 11468 (1969-05-10) replaced item (9) with a different office, which under the strike-and-insert ruling is an amendment (substance changed) and the clause continues, amended; EO 11581, EO 11604 and EO 11634 only renumbered items. Section 1 of EO 11708 places the Administrators of the Social and Rehabilitation Service, the National Institutes of Health and the Health Services and Mental Health Administration in level IV as new placements under its own text. I found no held instrument that ends any item earlier. research_rationale:
EO 8399 (signed 1940-04-29; 5 FR 1607, filed 1940-04-30) was read in full in the held Federal Register text layer. Acting under section 1753 of the Revised Statutes, it further amends the Executive Order of January 17, 1873, as amended (Executive Order No. 9, the prohibition on federal officers and employees holding state, territorial and municipal office), so as (1) to permit officers and employees of the Social Security Board, Federal Security Agency, on the Board's recommendation and the Federal Security Administrator's approval, to hold state, territorial and municipal office in cooperative work with the Board, and (2) to permit state, territorial and municipal officers engaged in that work to accept appointment under the Board, with civil-service appointments made under the civil-service laws. The two permissions are two clauses (the lead is folded into the first). The order states no expiry, condition or temporary term. EO 11408 (signed 1968-04-25) section 1 revoked Executive Order No. 9 of 1873 itself and section 2 revoked all prior orders insofar as they interpret or amend it, naming this order in its list of amendatory orders; because this order is wholly an amendment of the revoked order, both clauses first ended on 1968-04-25 by express revocation, which is also the whole-order end (the held text has no effective-date provision; the signing date is used). Open point disclosed for the reviewer: the Social Security Board named in both clauses was abolished by Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 1946, which is not held; no held source shows that the plan, or any other instrument, extinguished or ended these permissions before 1968, so the express revocation is the first documented end, and whether the permissions had already become inoperable in 1946 is not established.
